text:
tara (eng-sre): Heads-up: Careline is seeing repeated 502/503 + 429s on their Dedicated pool (eu-west-2-prod-pool-7). They report very spiky traffic causing the pool to scale up/down every ~90-150s and requests are timing out during transitions.

ben (oncall): @tara thanks. Any tenant IDs or sample request IDs? I can pull autoscaler events and traces. :eyes:

tara (eng-sre): tenant=careline-prod, sample request id=req_8a7f3c. Timeline: starts ~2026-03-17T12:03Z, spikes at 12:11 and 12:14, then heavy thrash from 12:18-12:30. They also mentioned intermittent 401s for a small subset of requests (maybe auth proxy issue?).

liam (support): Customer timeline matches our support ticket. They called out 200->0->200 scaling in logs. Also reported a jump in billable tokens at the same time (looks like retries).

ben (oncall): grabbing autoscaler events and pool timeline now. Quick look: scale events every 2m, cooldown currently 90s, policy="percent-add" with min=2 max=10. I'm seeing many short lived upscales then immediate downscale when request queue drains.

deploy-bot: [autoscaler][eu-west-2][pool-7] scale_up -> replicas=6 (+4) at 2026-03-17T12:18:06Z

deploy-bot: [autoscaler][eu-west-2][pool-7] scale_down -> replicas=2 (-4) at 2026-03-17T12:19:30Z

tara (eng-sre): Paste of relevant logs:```
[12:18:05Z] pool-7: enqueue request req_8a7f3c latency=18ms
[12:18:06Z] pool-7: scale_up triggered reason=queue_len>threshold target_replicas=6
[12:18:07Z] pool-7: node-launch ok id=i-0abc started 12:18:07Z
[12:19:28Z] pool-7: node-drain start id=i-0abc terminate 12:19:29Z
[12:19:30Z] pool-7: scale_down triggered reason=sustained_low_util target_replicas=2
[12:19:31Z] request req_8a7f3c timeout 30s status=502
```

anya (acct): Careline is enterprise, SLA > 99.9. They are on reserved capacity but this pool is shared multi-tenant (we reserved capacity but not pinned). They expect us to prioritize.

ben (oncall): Hypothesis: short spike -> autoscaler overshoots due to coarse percent-add, then quick drain causes immediate downscale. Combined with cold-start latency and retries this generates 502/429. Also seeing a few 401s — might be unrelated auth token expiry during retry storm.

tara (eng-sre): Short-term mitigations we can try now: 1) increase cooldown to 300s, 2) temporarily pin careline to dedicated slice (reserve 2 hot nodes), 3) enable soft rate-limit to reduce retry storms on edge, 4) bump min replicas to 4 for this pool. Which do we want first?

liam (support): Customer will accept short pin + cooldown change. They want us to avoid any downtime.

ben (oncall): I'll execute cooldown change + bump min replicas. Command:```
redwoodctl pool update eu-west-2 prod-pool-7 --cooldown=300s --min-replicas=4
```
I'll run in 2m and monitor. Adding a canary tag for careline traffic routing.

tara (eng-sre): Also turning on tenant-reserve for careline:```
redwoodctl tenant bind careline-prod --pool prod-pool-7 --reserve=2
```

ben (oncall): done. cooldown=300s, min-replicas=4 applied at 2026-03-17T12:22:10Z. Monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/pool7

sre-bot: [alert suppressed] Aggressive-scale-detect -> suppressed for pool-7 while cooldown > 180s

liam (support): Noted. Customer updated: they see fewer 502s so far but still occasional latency spikes (cold starts). They asked if we can pre-warm kernels for pinned nodes.

tara (eng-sre): Action items: ben will watch metrics for 30m, tara to open runbook PR to add recommended cooldown increase for percent-add policies, liam to keep customer updated, anya to confirm SLA and follow up on billing spike. If problems continue we'll consider dedicated single-tenant host for them. :shipit:

ben (oncall): Monitoring looks healthier after change. Queue length no longer oscillating, replica count stable at 4-6. I'll leave alerting sensitivity lowered for 30m and escalate if we see repeat oscillation.

liam (support): Customer sent logs showing auth failures tied to a token refresh race — forwarding to auth team (cc @tara).

tara (eng-sre): noted. I'll coordinate with auth. For posterity, adding repro steps for SRE playbook: 1) simulate 10s spike of 300 rps to pool/tenant, 2) observe scale events, 3) capture request ids and token header patterns.

anya (acct): Thanks all. Please keep me posted and add notes to the customer ticket.

ben (oncall): Follow-up: after 45m the error rate is down to baseline. Leaving this thread open for auth fix verification and a follow-up postmortem doc.

tara (eng-sre): I'll draft the postmortem and proposed autoscaler tuning table tomorrow. Closing in 24h if stable. :white_check_mark:
